'''Jaylen Nowell''' (born July 9, 1999<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaylen Nowell|work=Twitter.com|url=https://twitter.com/jaylennowell?lang=en|accessdate=March 12, 2019}}</ref>) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. He was a standout player at [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High School]] in Seattle.<ref name=lawson_01052018>{{cite news|last=Lawson|first=Theo|title=Washington State assistant, ex-Garfield coach Ed Haskins preparing for reunion with Washington’s Jaylen Nowell|date=January 5, 2018|newspaper=The Spokesman-Review|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/jan/05/washington-state-assistant-ex-garfield-coach-ed-ha/|accessdate=March 12, 2019}}</ref> Nowell was originally part of a five-player [[college recruiting|recruiting]] class considered the best in the Huskies' history. However, after Washington coach [[Lorenzo Romar]] was fired, he was the lone member who remained committed to the school and first-year coach [[Mike Hopkins (basketball)|Mike Hopkins]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Caple|first=Christian|title=Garfield's Nowell sticks with UW|date=April 18, 2017|newspaper=The News Tribune|url=https://www.kitsapsun.com/story/sports/college/2017/04/18/garfields-nowell-sticks-uw/100628974/|accessdate=March 12, 2019}}</ref> As a freshman in [[2017–18 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|2017–18]], Nowell averaged 16.0 points per game.<ref>{{cite news|last=Calkins|first=Matt|title=Huskies star Jaylen Nowell has gotten even better — and smarter|date=January 17, 2019|newspaper=The Seattle Times|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/calkins-column-on-uw-basketball-player-jaylen-nowell/|accessdate=March 12, 2019}}</ref> The [[2018–19 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|following season]], he was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] after leading the Huskies in scoring and helping them win the Pac-12 regular season championship.<ref>{{cite news|last=Allen|first=Percy|title=Huskies win top three Pac-12 postseason awards: Jaylen Nowell is player of the year|date=March 11, 2019|newspaper=The Seattle Times|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/uws-matisse-thybulle-and-jaylen-nowell-voted-first-team-all-pac-12/|accessdate=March 12, 2019}}</ref>

Nowell is the son of Lanie and Mike Nowell. They met at [[Clark Atlanta University]], where they both played basketball.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hamilton|first=Brian|title='His game screams': Why Washington’s Jaylen Nowell can’t stop|date=March 6, 2019|work=The Athletic|url=https://theathletic.com/849840/2019/03/06/his-game-screams-why-washingtons-jaylen-nowell-cant-stop/|accessdate=March 12, 2019|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His father played professionally in the [[Continental Basketball Association]].<ref name=lawson_01052018/>

Following Washington's loss in the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Nowell announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA Draft]], where he has been projected to be anywhere from a mid first-round to a second-round selection.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26412282/washington-guard-nowell-declares-nba-draft|title=Washington guard Nowell declares for NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|date=March 31, 2019}}</ref>
